answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger works like a prism: each agent's history is split into verifiable work records, and a newcomer must forge trust by locking a deposit and completing small paid tasks before handling larger ones. When a tide of fresh identities arrives, the system raises the entry bond and slows onboarding, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand deposits and a thousand task costs, while honest agents earn their bond back through good work. Sybil scale becomes expensive, not free.
